Drugs 1988; 35: 604–45. 2. Lamb HM, et al. Ceftriaxone: an update of its use in the manage- ment of community-acquired and nosocomial infections. Drugs 2002; 62: 1041–89. 3. Bijie H, et al. Administration in hepatic and renal impairment. A re- duction in dosage of ceftriaxone may be necessary in patients with severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance below 10 mL/minute), in whom the daily dose should not exceed 2 g. In patients undergoing dialysis, and in those with both renal and hepatic impairment, plasma concentrations of ceftriaxone should be monitored to determine whether dose adjustment is needed.
